prompt: Make a square 1080x1080 social media card announcing a free community workshop, Intro to Bread Baking, on Saturday, March 14 at 10:00 am at the Eastmoor Library, community room B. It is free, people should bring an apron, and they can sign up at eastmoor.example/bread. Keep it friendly.
prompt_suffix: Return the result as a single self-contained HTML file: all CSS inline, no external requests, system fonts only. Reply with one ```html fenced block and nothing else.
rubric: The workshop title is clearly the dominant element and is much larger than every other piece of text.
The date, time and place are easy to find, grouped together, and use no more than about three levels of emphasis overall.
Lines are set comfortably: sensible line length and line-height, no awkward one-word last lines, and no clipped or cramped text.
The card uses a small, consistent set of type styles (one or two families, few sizes and weights) with consistent alignment.
All text, including the smallest line, has strong contrast and is readable at phone size.
featuring_rule: Declared before any run: rank the 3 without-skill runs and the 3 with-skill runs separately by the blind judge's rubric mean (two passes with the sides swapped, scores averaged), and feature the median run of each arm. The best run is never chosen. The contact sheet shows all six runs.

pairs.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A's title is larger and more commanding, and it fills the square well. The date, time and place sit in clear cards with strong contrast, though the 'Sign Up Now!' line is cramped and the cards add several levels of emphasis. B is clean and consistent, but its content is small and floats in a lot of empty space. Its small labels and salmon URL have weaker contrast, and the orange time adds an extra level of emphasis to the details block. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has a calmer layout: the date, time and place sit together in one centered stack, and it uses few type styles. Its weak points are the small text floating in a lot of empty space and the faint brown labels and coral URL, which are low-contrast on the beige background. B has a larger title and better contrast on its white cards, but it feels crowded: 'Sign Up Now!' is jammed between two boxes, the time is set very small, and the card mixes more styles (italic text, badges, emoji labels, outlined and filled boxes).

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both cards leave out the sign-up URL. B fits everything comfortably in the frame and groups when, where, cost and what to bring into one clean, aligned block. A has a bigger, more dominant title, but its card runs off the bottom edge, there's a lot of uneven empty space, and the tan 'FREE' text and the tiny WHEN/WHERE labels are low-contrast. B's white-on-tan chips are also weak on contrast, but its layout is more consistent and easier to read overall. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Neither card shows the sign-up URL eastmoor.example/bread, and both repeat FREE and use some low-contrast white-on-tan text. B's title is more dominant and its When/Where blocks are clearer, but it switches from left-aligned to centered text and the card runs off the bottom edge. A is the tidier and more consistent of the two: one centered composition with all the details in a single box.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both cards make the title the largest text, but in each it is only about twice the size of the date. A keeps the date, time, place and what-to-bring together in one card with consistent type, and every line is dark enough to read. B puts the date and location in two separate wide boxes and uses more text sizes, from the very small DATE & TIME and LOCATION labels and 'Learn more:' up to the title. B's sign-up URL is light tan on cream and the button text is white on light tan, both weak in contrast, while A's dark URL is small but readable. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both cards make the title clearly dominant and group the event details well, but B puts date, time, location and what to bring in one card, which is tighter and easier to scan. A's most important action line, the URL, is light tan on cream, and its white-on-tan button is also low contrast; A also leaves a large empty gap above the button. B's URL is small and italic, and its grey labels are a bit light, but its text reads better overall at phone size.
